topic: Why sunsets are red when the sky is blue
title: Why Sunsets Are Red When the Sky Is Blue
hook_promise: Why the same sky is blue at noon and red at sunset: at sunset the light takes a longer path through the air, and the blue is scattered away.

beats.narration: Blue all day, then red at sunset? What changed?
beats.visual_intent: Two friends at a café table look through a tall window where the sky glows blue on one side and orange on the other.

shot.image_prompt: Sunlit café, wide shot. Lead and friend sit at the round wooden table facing a tall window. Through the glass the sky is deep blue at the top and glows orange near the rooftops. Green coffee cups on the table, ivy, terracotta tiles, warm dappled light. Both look curious and a little puzzled.

beats.narration: Sunlight hits the air, and molecules scatter it in every direction. That's called Rayleigh scattering.
beats.visual_intent: A sunbeam through the café window lights up drifting dust specks that bounce light in all directions.

shot.image_prompt: Close insert of a golden sunbeam slanting through a tall café window, glowing specks of dust drifting and catching the light in every direction. Blurred green plant and wooden chair edge in the background. Warm, soft light.

beats.narration: But colors scatter unequally. Short wavelengths get scattered far more than long ones.
beats.visual_intent: On the table, a small blue ball bounces wildly with motion trails while a red ball just rolls straight.

shot.image_prompt: Medium shot at the café round table. A small blue ball bounces and ricochets with curved painted motion trails; a red ball beside it rolls calmly in a straight line. Lead points at the blue ball, friend watches with raised brows. Warm golden light, green cups at the edge.
pose_variants: Lead leans in with both mitten hands on the table, eyes on the blue ball, smiling.

beats.narration: So why not violet? The sun puts out much more blue, so blue wins.
beats.visual_intent: The friend shrugs at the violet question while the lead nods, with a blue ball sitting bigger than a violet ball between them.

shot.image_prompt: Close shot of lead and friend at the café table. A large glowing blue ball and a much smaller violet ball sit between them. Friend looks quizzical with hands raised; lead has a knowing small smile. Soft golden light, ivy behind.
pose_variants: Friend with open palms raised in a shrug, brows lifted.
Friend with a hand on chin, thinking.

beats.narration: At sunset, the sun sits low. Its light crosses much more air.
beats.visual_intent: On a street corner at dusk, the low sun sends a long beam across a big stretch of hazy sky as the friends watch.

shot.image_prompt: Wide street-corner scene in late-afternoon light. A big sun hangs low just above the rooftops, its beam stretching across a wide band of hazy golden sky toward the two figures. Lead and friend stand on the pavement; lead points up at the sun. Long soft shadows, warm dappled light.

beats.narration: On that long trip, most blue is scattered out. Mostly red is left.
beats.visual_intent: A close-up of the lead's face lit in deep orange as the blue drains out of the sky behind.

shot.image_prompt: Close shot of the lead's round white head in profile, lit with deep orange-red glow from a low sun. Behind, the sky fades from faint blue at the top to rich red at the horizon. Quiet, wondering expression. Warm painterly light.

beats.narration: The red isn't added. The blue is taken away.
beats.visual_intent: A glass jar of blue and red marbles sits on a bench; the lead reaches in and the blue ones are removed, leaving red.

shot.image_prompt: Medium shot of lead and friend on a street bench in golden dusk light. Between them a glass jar holds mostly red marbles with a few blue ones left; lead reaches toward it, friend watches with interest. Warm light, soft shadows.
pose_variants: Lead holds up a single blue marble between mitten fingers, examining it.
Lead sits back with hands in lap, smiling at the jar.

beats.narration: Mars flips it. NASA rovers show a reddish day sky, and a blue-gray sunset.
beats.visual_intent: The friend holds up a painted photograph of a rusty-orange Martian sky with a blue glow around the sun.

shot.image_prompt: Insert shot: friend's mitten hands hold up a painted photo of an orange-red desert sky over rocky ground, with a cool blue-gray glow around a small sun near the horizon. Teal scarf in frame edge, blurred warm street behind.

beats.narration: Short path, you see scattered blue. Long path, only red survives.
beats.visual_intent: Both friends stand at the dusk street, lead pointing from the high blue sky down to the low red sun.

shot.image_prompt: Wide street shot at dusk. The sky above is soft blue, shifting to deep red-orange around a low sun. Lead and friend stand side by side; lead points toward the red horizon, friend nods. Warm painterly light, long shadows.

beats.narration: Next sunset, watch the blue leave. Blue all day, then red.
beats.visual_intent: Back at the café, the friends sit quietly watching the window turn from blue to orange.

shot.image_prompt: Medium shot in the sunlit café. Lead and friend sit at the round wooden table, green cups before them, gazing at the tall window where the sky glows orange-red over the rooftops. Calm, content expressions, dappled golden light, ivy and hanging lamp.

sources.claim: The sky is not violet because the sun puts out much more blue light than violet light, so most of the scattered light in the sky is blue.
sources.title: Blue Sky: Waves & Light Science Activity
sources.quote: The sun puts out much more blue light than violet light, so most of the scattered light in the sky is blue.

sources.claim: At sunrise or sunset, when the Sun is close to the horizon, its light must travel through more of the atmosphere than when the Sun is overhead.
